label: NECESSARILY_POSSIBLY_2: Kripke necessity over a frame: □φ holds at w when φ holds at every world…
term: necessarily / possibly (□, ◇ of the QML KB embedding; Lean `Box`, `Dia`)
definition: Kripke necessity over a frame (`TruthCore.Modal.Frame`): □φ holds at w when φ holds at every world accessible from w, ◇φ when at some. The embedding's frame and domain assumptions, as in the AFP theory: accessibility is constrained only by symmetry (axiom sym, logic KB; no reflexivity); quantifiers over individuals range over the whole type at every world (possibilist, constant domain, no existence predicate), so 'exists' in T3 and C2 is that quantifier; properties are intensional (`Ind → World → Prop`) and quantification over them ranges over every such function (full comprehension); validity [_] is truth at every world; the host logic is classical, which the Lean results take as the explicit premise STMT-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE.
note: Operator/framework distinction (#1111): Box and Dia themselves require only the supplied Frame; their declarations assume no symmetry, reflexivity, domain policy, comprehension or excluded middle. The sourced KB embedding context above states separate commitments, not extra conjuncts of the operator definition. DEF-MODAL-FIXTURE-FRAME uses that same Box with arbitrary frames. NecessaryAt in DEF-KANT-MODAL-NECESSITY is Box applied to one fixed individual’s existence predicate under the identical frame; that exact equality transfers no KB frame law or historical/source identity.
